prompt: In rag.py, where does the question's vector come from?
hint: The same SDK, a different model.

choices.text: The chat model's reply
choices.why: The chat model runs after the search.

choices.text: pgvector computes it from the question text
choices.why: pgvector stores and compares vectors; it embeds nothing.

choices.text: A copy of the index's vectors kept in the program
choices.why: The question is new; its vector has to be made for it.

choices.text: Ollama's embedding endpoint, from all-minilm
choices.why: Right: the same SDK and the same server serve both models.

prompt: Why does rag.py have no reranker?

choices.text: Rerankers do not work on results that pgvector returns
choices.why: A reranker runs after any search.

choices.text: The SDK cannot call two models
choices.why: It already calls two.

choices.text: The reranker this machine can run lost every identifier
choices.why: Right: a step is added when a measurement asks for it, and this one asked against it.

choices.text: Reranking would break the citations
choices.why: Citations number whatever order is sent.

prompt: A team points rag.py at a real provider and changes the embedding model to the provider's own, leaving the index as it is. What happens?

choices.text: Questions meet vectors from another model
choices.why: Right: the index must be rebuilt with the new model first.

choices.text: pgvector refuses the query
choices.why: Only if the dimensions differ; the meanings still would.

choices.text: The floor adjusts itself
choices.why: Nothing adjusts the floor.

choices.text: It works, since only the chat model matters
choices.why: The question's vector must come from the index's model.

prompt: What did Ollama answer when documents.py asked for document citations?

choices.text: A 400 error naming the citations field
choices.why: Right: its Messages API has no document citations, and it says so.

choices.text: A reply with character ranges
choices.why: That is what Anthropic's own API returns; Ollama refused.

choices.text: A reply with [n] numbers in the text
choices.why: That was rag_claude.py, which sends numbered text.

choices.text: A reply that ignored the documents
choices.why: That was the second run, without the citations field.

prompt: Without the citations field, the request with document blocks was accepted and read 42 tokens in all. What does that say?

choices.text: Ollama dropped the document blocks without saying so
choices.why: Right: 42 tokens is the system message and the question, and the reply knew nothing of Marginalia.

choices.text: The documents were cached and cost nothing
choices.why: A cached token is still counted, as cache_read_input_tokens.

choices.text: The model summarised the documents first
choices.why: Input tokens count what was read; three sources are hundreds.

choices.text: Anthropic's encoding is ten times denser
choices.why: The same sources as plain text came to 336.

prompt: With provider citations giving exact character ranges, what does the lesson say a legal pipeline should still do?
hint: A span is a claim too.

choices.text: Confirm the text is in the source at those characters
choices.why: Right: one string comparison with the span in hand.

choices.text: Switch back to Chat Completions
choices.why: The format is not the issue.

choices.text: Nothing more; the provider guarantees the span
choices.why: The span is where the provider says the text came from.

choices.text: Re-embed the cited sentence
choices.why: Similarity is not the check needed here.

prompt: In how many pieces did the streamed reply arrive?
What does streaming NOT shorten?
hint: Nothing streams until the prompt exists.

choices.text: The wait for the whole reply to be written
choices.why: It hides that wait by showing words as they come.

choices.text: The retrieval time
choices.why: Right: the search still finishes before anything streams.

choices.text: The time to the first word on screen
choices.why: That is exactly what it shortens.

choices.text: The time the customer stares at a blank box
choices.why: That is what it improves.

prompt: Why does a streamed reply complicate lesson 7's citation check?

choices.text: The SDK forbids reading a streamed reply twice
choices.why: The program can keep the text it printed.

choices.text: It needs the whole reply, which arrives last
choices.why: Right: show as it arrives, then annotate, or hold it back.

choices.text: Streamed replies have no citations
choices.why: They do; the markers stream with the text.

choices.text: Streaming changes the sources
choices.why: The sources are fixed before streaming starts.

prompt: To receive token counts in a streamed Chat Completions reply, the request sets stream_options with include____.
fragile.py gives the client one second. What did the SDK do when the chat request took longer?

choices.text: Raised APITimeoutError at once
choices.why: It retried first: the log shows two retries.

choices.text: Waited for the reply however long it took
choices.why: The timeout is one second per attempt.

choices.text: Retried twice with a growing wait, then raised APITimeoutError
choices.why: Right: three attempts in all, each starting the generation again.

choices.text: Retried the embedding request instead
choices.why: The embedding answered 200 OK within the second.

prompt: Why is a timeout that is too short worse than a failure?
hint: What does each retry start again?

choices.text: It hides the error from the log
choices.why: OPENAI_LOG showed every retry.

choices.text: Each retry starts the generation again, for an answer nobody receives
choices.why: Right: three generations' worth of the machine, and the customer still waits.

choices.text: The SDK disables retries after one timeout
choices.why: It retried twice.

choices.text: The floor refuses the question
choices.why: The search succeeded; the floor was passed.

prompt: The chat call fails after a successful search. What does the lesson suggest showing the customer?

choices.text: The refusal sentence
choices.why: That says the documents do not cover it, which is false.

choices.text: A loop of retries that runs until one succeeds
choices.why: Unbounded retries leave the customer waiting.

choices.text: A stack trace, so the customer can report it
choices.why: That is an accident, not a decision.

choices.text: The retrieved articles, with no answer
choices.why: Right: the sources are known and useful.

prompt: Match each failure to whether the SDK retries it.

pairs.right: not retried, since repeating cannot help

prompt: With a budget of 250, how many tokens did the prompt use?
Why does budget.py drop whole sources instead of cutting the last one to fit?

choices.text: It is faster to drop than to cut
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: A half source loses its second half, the exception
choices.why: Right: every source stays intact.

choices.text: Cutting text breaks the tokenizer
choices.why: Any text can be tokenized.

choices.text: Providers refuse partial sources
choices.why: A provider cannot tell.

prompt: budget.py counts with tiktoken's cl100k_base, and Ollama reports its own count, which includes the template it wraps around every message. What does the lesson conclude?

choices.text: Ollama overcounts
choices.why: It counts with llama3.2's own tokenizer, which is the count that fills the window.

choices.text: The local count is wrong and should not be used
choices.why: It is close enough to budget with.

choices.text: Tokens cannot be counted before sending
choices.why: budget.py did exactly that.

choices.text: Budget with a margin, never to the last token
choices.why: Right: a count by one tokenizer is an estimate of another's.

prompt: Why does the lesson want a budget far below the model's window?

choices.text: Models refuse prompts above half their window
choices.why: They accept anything that fits.

choices.text: Price, time and distraction hold at any size
choices.why: Right: the window is a maximum, not a target.

choices.text: Larger prompts are cached less
choices.why: Caching is lesson 17's subject and not the reason.

choices.text: pgvector cannot return more chunks
choices.why: It returns whatever LIMIT asks.

prompt: Which field of the query log lets the floor be adjusted from real questions?

choices.text: completion_tokens
choices.why: That is cost.

choices.text: cited
choices.why: That shows which chunks are used.

choices.text: reply
choices.why: The reply helps review, not the floor.

choices.text: sources, with their scores
choices.why: Right.

prompt: Why does the lesson treat the query log as personal data?
hint: What do customers type into support chats?

choices.text: It contains embeddings
choices.why: It contains chunk ids and scores, not vectors.

choices.text: The provider requires it
choices.why: It is the law and the privacy notice, not the provider.

choices.text: Every log is personal data
choices.why: This one is because of what customers type.

choices.text: Questions hold names, order numbers and addresses
choices.why: Right: it needs retention, deletion and restricted access.

prompt: A chunk has not been cited once in a month of logged queries. What does the lesson say that tells you?

choices.text: The floor is too low
choices.why: A low floor admits more chunks, not fewer.

choices.text: Nobody asks, or the search never finds it
choices.why: Right: both are worth knowing.

choices.text: It should be deleted from the index at once
choices.why: It may be about something rare and still right.

choices.text: Its stored embedding has been corrupted somewhere
choices.why: Possible but not what the lesson draws from it.

prompt: rag.py appends one JSON line per query to the file queries.___.
Put what ask() in rag.py does in order.
items: Retrieve the sources above the floor
Generate a reply, or refuse if there are none

prompt: Which change to rag.py would lesson 9 call premature?
hint: Steps are added when a measurement asks.

choices.text: A semantic cache before repeats are measured
choices.why: Right: lesson 17 measures that first.

choices.text: Setting an explicit timeout on the client it creates
choices.why: The default timeout is nobody's choice; setting one is not premature.

choices.text: Refusing questions whose best source is below the floor
choices.why: That was measured in lessons 6 to 8.

choices.text: Logging each query with its sources and scores
choices.why: The log is what later measurements need.

prompt: Which of these did this lesson's runs show? Choose all that apply.

choices.why: Yes: 42 tokens read, and a reply about gift cards in general.

choices.text: A budget of 250 keeping one source of three
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A streamed reply's first token arriving in under 100 ms
choices.why: No timing was quoted.

choices.text: A chat request retried twice after a timeout
choices.why: Yes: fragile.py's log.

choices.text: Anthropic citations with character ranges
